players.product: probe cards for HBM/DRAM wafer test

quarterly_data.signal: DRAM MIX, Q4 VS Q1 (CEO): Q4 DRAM probe cards delivered the expected sequential growth 'to a new record, with the increase coming from non-HBM DRAM applications like DDR4 and DDR5'. For Q1 FormFactor again expects 'an all-time DRAM record, this time on HBM strength, with contributions from both sustained demand in HBM3E and the early stages of the HBM4 ramp.' Asked for an HBM dollar amount, the CEO said: 'if in Q4, it was kinda mid-forties. Think of it as a low fifties kind of number for Q1 based on where we currently sit.' He gave no view on the HBM vs DDR mix beyond near-term visibility: 'Our customers are wafer start constrained. And they're making choices every day of whether they start HBM wafers, HBM core die wafers, or a DDR5 or a DDR4 part.' Lead times are still 'well within a quarter', but visibility for the more complex DRAM cards now extends to the end of the quarter (six, seven, eight-week visibility). He expects memory, 'DRAM in particular, to continue to grow', citing 'both major ATE manufacturers having very robust forecasts and views of 2026', and FormFactor is investing to expand both its competitive advantage and its capacity in DRAM.
quarterly_data.figure: HBM probe-card revenue 'kinda mid-forties' in Q4 and 'a low fifties kind of number for Q1' (answer to a dollar-amount question); Q4 DRAM record on DDR4/DDR5; Q1 all-time DRAM record on HBM3E + early HBM4

quarterly_data.signal: HBM4 RAISES TEST INTENSITY AND COMPLEXITY (CEO): 'the test intensity for each HBM stack further increases with the transition to HBM4 16-high stacks of core die chiplets, up from the 8 and 12-high stacks of HBM3 and 3E', resulting in 'higher probe card spending by our customers for HBM applications'. 'The overall stack bandwidth of HBM4 more than doubles HBM3 to an astounding 2+ terabits per second.' SmartMatrix is 'the industry's only production-proven probe card architecture that combines high parallelism productivity with high-speed test capability', letting customers 'test hundreds of die simultaneously at the 10 gigabit plus IO data rate of HBM4.' Rule of thumb for each generational step: 'maybe 20, 25% on a like-for-like same stack out basis is not a bad way to think about the test intensity as we go from HBM generation to HBM generation', with rising customer yields as a partial offset.
quarterly_data.figure: HBM4 16-high stacks (vs 8 and 12-high for HBM3 and 3E); HBM4 stack bandwidth 2+ terabits per second; 10 gigabit plus IO; test intensity maybe 20, 25% higher per HBM generation

quarterly_data.signal: HBM5 ROADMAP (CEO): FormFactor's R&D and engineering teams are partnering with customers to advance SmartMatrix 'to meet the challenging specifications for HBM5 and beyond'; 'HBM5 bandwidth is projected to double again over HBM4.' 'HBM5 is a couple of years away from volume production', but complex R&D and capacity must be ready early. The inflections he expects: layer height ('HBM4 gets to 16 high. We'll see whether HBM5 continues to climb'); 'new packaging and stacking techniques like hybrid bonding are certainly a potential for HBM5', which he called interesting for FormFactor 'because we have tremendous know-how on probing on copper', and copper is 'an important part of a hybrid bonding flow'; and higher speeds, most recently 'this 11 gigabit per second spec for HBM4', which must be tested at high parallelism while handling power and thermal challenges.
quarterly_data.figure: HBM5 a couple of years away from volume production; HBM5 bandwidth projected to double again over HBM4; 11 gigabit per second spec for HBM4

quarterly_data.signal: HBM SHARE GAINS AT ALL THREE MAKERS (CEO): SmartMatrix's combination of high parallelism and high speed 'is producing market share gains at all three major HBM manufacturers', part of a strategy 'to be a key supplier to all the leading customers in the industry', although 'our first quarter HBM revenue continues to be skewed towards our largest customer, consistent with the current market share split between our customers.' FormFactor has 'a very strong share position as our number one customer' and is using SmartMatrix 'as a beachhead' to raise share at the other two HBM manufacturers, where its incumbent share is 'relatively low'; 'there's really only two suppliers that can do anything close to this.' A share position like the one at the number-one customer is unlikely there, but it is 'a significant opportunity'. Share at the other two was not quantified; asked whether FormFactor is the number-two source at those two, the CEO answered 'From an overall DRAM standpoint.' No customer is named on the call.

players.product: CPO / silicon-photonics wafer test - insertion-1 known-good-die probe on PIC wafers, plus engineering probers

quarterly_data.signal: CPO TEST AND THE KEYSTONE PHOTONICS DEAL (CEO/IR): Systems revenue rose sequentially in Q4 as expected, 'driven by customer investment in co-package optics and quantum computing'. A typical seasonal decline is expected in Q1, and Systems is going through 'a bit of a transition as we start to ramp up CPO'. CPO 'continues to be a primary area of focus for us, as it represents an exciting growth opportunity where we have a strong leadership position.' In December FormFactor acquired Keystone Photonics, whose optical probe technology 'enables high-efficiency optical coupling to our customers' photonic devices', complementing FormFactor's advanced MEMS electrical probes. Together with the CM300XI and Triton test platforms, it 'expands FormFactor's leadership position' in CPO test. FormFactor used about $20 million in cash for the deal, described as 'a key element of our co-packaged optics product roadmap.' Systems segment gross margin declined 50 basis points in Q4.
quarterly_data.figure: about $20 million in cash to acquire Keystone Photonics (December); Q4 Systems up sequentially on CPO and quantum computing; Q1 seasonal decline

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 RESULTS (CEO/CFO/IR): Q4 revenue, gross margin and EPS all exceeded Q3 and the high end of the outlook range, with record revenue 'on both a quarterly and annual basis.' Q4 2025 revenues of $215.2 million came in at the high end of the $205 million to $215 million outlook. GAAP gross margin was 42.2% (39.8% in Q3); non-GAAP gross margin was 43.9%, 290 basis points above the 41% in Q3, driven by probe card segment margins up 364 basis points to 44.5% and partly offset by Systems, down 50 basis points. GAAP net income was $23.2 million ($0.29 per diluted share); non-GAAP net income was $36.6 million ($0.46). Free cash flow was $34.7 million (vs $19.7 million in Q3) and operating cash flow $46 million. Cash and investments ended at $275 million after about $20 million for Keystone Photonics. No shares were repurchased; cash is prioritized for the Farmers Branch ramp.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 2025 revenues of $215.2 million (outlook $205 million to $215 million); GAAP GM 42.2%; non-GAAP GM 43.9% (41% in Q3); non-GAAP EPS $0.46; free cash flows $34.7 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2026 OUTLOOK (CFO/CEO): Q1 revenues of $225 million plus or minus $5 million; non-GAAP gross margin 45% plus or minus 150 basis points, with 'about a 200 basis point impact to gross margins from tariffs'; non-GAAP opex $62 million plus or minus $2 million (about $4.5 million above Q4, mainly Farmers Branch start-up costs); non-GAAP EPS $0.45 plus or minus $0.04. Mix (CEO): Systems is expected down seasonally 'as we start to ramp up CPO', so probe cards grow by more than $10 million, 'roughly equal parts of foundry and logic. And DRAM', with the DRAM step-up coming from HBM. FormFactor will present its next target financial model at an Analyst Day on May 11.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenues of $225 million plus or minus $5 million; non-GAAP GM 45% plus or minus 150 basis points; non-GAAP EPS $0.45 plus or minus $0.04; opex $62 million plus or minus $2 million

quarterly_data.signal: GROSS-MARGIN PATH (CFO/CEO): 'Q2 2025 gross margins were 38.5%'; through Q4 2025 FormFactor generated 'a cumulative improvement of 540 basis points', with another 110 basis points expected in Q1 2026 at the guidance midpoint. About two-thirds of the 540 basis points came from cost initiatives (shorter cycle times, higher yields, the workforce reduction) and the rest from volume. The target model is '47% margins at $850 million a year run rate for revenue', excluding tariffs; '45% is what we're targeting as long as we have a 200 basis point tariff headwind', which FormFactor expects to reach within 2026 while it pursues tariff drawbacks whose benefit 'could be several quarters' away. Further gains in 2026 will come 'at a more moderate pace'. On pricing (CEO): 'if there's a specific program that's super important for a customer, and valuable for their time to market, we're able to share in that value as well', though not across the board; the CFO said pricing is not the main path for margin improvement.
quarterly_data.figure: cumulative improvement of 540 basis points since Q2 2025 (38.5%); target model 47% margins at $850 million a year run rate; 45% targeted with a 200 basis point tariff headwind; about two-thirds from cost initiatives

quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY AND FARMERS BRANCH (CFO/CEO): After the yield and cycle-time work, 'we believe we now have the ability to execute at a run rate of $225 million a quarter' from the existing footprint, and more output will be squeezed out through 2026 in smaller steps. The Farmers Branch site will 'begin to come online later this year and to ramp over the course of 2027', on schedule for the end of the year with 'no changes to that timeline', at 'a structurally lower cost', and is expected to be accretive to gross margins once the ramp is complete. Pre-production opex is roughly $6 million in Q1 2026 (vs $1.7 million in Q4 2025) and between $20 million and $25 million over 2026. Industry capacity is tight too: '70% of probe card market shares owned by three of us', and FormFactor's primary competitors in Foundry and Logic and in DRAM 'have all been transparent about the need and the initiatives to add capacity'. FormFactor will 'capture some incremental market share if we can just with the ability to deliver.' Visibility remains short, 'within a quarter'.
quarterly_data.figure: run rate of $225 million a quarter from the existing footprint; Farmers Branch to ramp over the course of 2027; pre-production opex roughly $6 million in Q1 2026, between $20 million and $25 million over 2026; 70% of probe card market shares owned by three players

quarterly_data.signal: FOUNDRY & LOGIC PIVOTS TO THE DATA CENTER (CEO): Q4 foundry and logic demand was comparable to Q3. Q1 demand is expected to rise, and that growth is 'not anticipated to come from our historical drivers of client PC and mobile, but instead from a significant shift toward rapidly growing data center applications like network switches.' 'As our top customer historically, a large microprocessor IDM was not a 10% customer in either the fourth quarter or for 2025 overall', even as FormFactor posted record revenue in both periods. FormFactor continues to support that customer's turnaround 'as well as their effort to become a leading foundry' and expects to grow with it, and is building 'the foundation for market share gains at a large fabless CPU manufacturer.' Management expects the foundry and logic market to grow in 2026 and FormFactor to gain share there; it already has strong positions in networking. No customer is named on the call.
quarterly_data.figure: historical top customer (a large microprocessor IDM) not a 10% customer in Q4 or 2025; Q1 foundry and logic growth from data-center network switches

quarterly_data.signal: GPU AND CUSTOM ASIC PROBE CARDS (CEO): The production qualification in leading-edge GPU applications is in its reliability-test phase, with cards 'being run, you know, with hundreds of wafers, multiple touchdowns', and 'we continue to expect to generate revenue from this merchant GPU call in the second half of the year.' Sizing: the merchant GPU opportunity 'probably was a $50 million spend primarily with our competitor in Foundry and Logic in 2025. That may be conservative.' Custom ASIC: after a 'multimillion-dollar mid-2025 design win', FormFactor is 'now seeing the second leg of that for some recently announced custom ASIC', and engagements with 'the hyperscalers and their ASIC design partners' are deepening; this opportunity is harder to size. For GPU, custom ASIC and in-rack networking (scale-up and scale-out) combined, he estimated 'hundreds of millions of dollars of SAM for all of those different things in 2025', growing in 2026 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: merchant GPU probe-card spend 'probably was a $50 million spend' in 2025 (may be conservative); GPU revenue expected in the second half; hundreds of millions of dollars of SAM for GPU, custom ASIC and networking in 2025
